name: Stovetop Cooking
summary: Searing, sautéing, pan-frying and simmering: choosing a pan and oil, heat levels, and a quick pan sauce.

rows: A deep brown crust on steaks, chops, chicken, scallops. A thin film of oil, food left alone.
Small pieces (vegetables, shrimp, sliced meat) cooked fast in a little fat, stirred or tossed often.
Like sautéing, faster and hotter, stirring constantly. Prep everything first: there's no time once it starts.
Cutlets, fish, breaded food in about ¼ inch (6 mm) of oil, turned once.
Soups, stews, sauces, grains. Small bubbles breaking the surface now and then.
Eggs, fish, chicken in liquid that's steaming but barely bubbling, for tender, moist results.
Pasta, potatoes, blanching vegetables. Big, rolling bubbles.

items: Take the meat out of the fridge 20–30 minutes ahead and pat it very dry: a wet surface steams instead of browning.
Heat a heavy pan (cast iron or stainless) over medium-high to high for 2–3 minutes.
Add a thin film of high-smoke-point oil; when it shimmers, add the meat, laying it away from you.
Leave it alone until it releases easily and is deep brown, usually 2–4 minutes, then turn it.
Thick pieces: finish in a 400°F (200°C) oven or lower the heat, and check with a thermometer.

blocks.text: Don't crowd the pan. Leave a finger's width between pieces and cook in batches; too much food at once cools the pan and everything turns gray.

rows: Searing, pan-frying, cornbread, going from stove to oven. Holds heat like nothing else.
Long-simmered acidic sauces (tomato, wine) in a newly seasoned pan; soaking it.
Searing, sautéing, pan sauces (the browned bits stick, then lift off with liquid). Dishwasher-safe.
Eggs and delicate fish unless you're generous with fat and patience.
High heat (keep it at medium or below) and metal tools.

sections.heading: Oils and smoke points
blocks: Every fat starts to smoke at some point, and past it, it tastes acrid. Match the fat to the heat.

items: **High heat** (searing, stir-frying, deep-frying): vegetable, canola, peanut, avocado or refined sunflower oil.
**Medium heat** (sautéing, roasting): olive oil, including extra-virgin, is fine for everyday sautéing.
**Low heat or flavor** (finishing, eggs, sauces): butter. For searing with butter, start in oil and add the butter near the end.

sections.heading: A quick pan sauce
blocks: After searing, the browned bits (fond) stuck to the pan are flavor. Turn them into a sauce while the meat rests:

items: Pour off all but a spoonful of fat. Over medium heat, cook a chopped shallot or garlic clove for 30 seconds.
Add about ½ cup (120 ml) of wine, stock or even water and scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon.
Simmer until reduced by about half, then turn off the heat.
Swirl in a tablespoon of cold butter, add any juices from the resting meat, and season with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon or a little mustard.

sections.heading: Deep-frying safely
blocks: Use a heavy, deep pot filled no more than halfway with a high-smoke-point oil, and a thermometer clipped to the side. Most frying happens at 350–375°F (175–190°C). Fry in small batches so the temperature doesn't crash, and lower food in gently with a spider or slotted spoon.

blocks.text: Never leave hot oil unattended, and keep water away from it. If oil catches fire, turn off the heat and slide a lid or baking sheet over the pot. Never use water: it makes burning oil explode.
